_note: PLAN.md 9. All numbers are STARTING VALUES to be tuned by playtest.
MVP is two buildings (PLAN.md 10): a Town Centre to train from and a House
to raise the pop cap. Barracks and the dragon nest are later phases.
Each building names THREE visuals, not one. A building is a foundation, a
completed structure, or rubble (SimBuilding.Phase), and 0 A.D. models those
as separate actors -- so they are separate atlases, shared by footprint size:
vis.foundation_8x8 will serve every 8x8 building added later. There is no
under-construction art; the foundation covers that phase too, and 5.2 shows
progress by clipping the completed sprite over it (ASSET_MISSING.md 1.2).
FOOTPRINTS COME FROM THE MEASURED ART, not from PLAN.md 9's sketch, which
wrote [4, 4] for the town centre before anything had been measured. Measured
via `isobake inspect`, halved to project metres, divided by the 2 m tile:
town centre   15.53 x 15.00 m  = 7.77 tiles  -> [8, 8]
house         10.00 x 10.00 m  = 5.00 tiles  -> [4, 4]   (see below)
The town centre also agrees with 0 A.D.'s own 30x30-unit obstruction and with
the fndn_8x8 foundation their template pairs it with. Scaling the mesh down
to fit a smaller footprint is not the alternative -- it would break the
one-global-pixels_per_metre rule (PLAN.md 2.2) and leave a villager taller
than the doorway.
The house is the one place art and gameplay deliberately DISAGREE: the mesh
is 5 tiles across but the footprint is [4, 4], matching the 4x4 foundation
0 A.D. pairs it with. So the roof overhangs its own tiles by half a tile a
side. That is the right trade -- a 5x5 house is oddly large next to an 8x8
town centre, odd-sized footprints centre badly on a grid, and overhanging
roofs are normal in isometric RTS art. Revisit if placement collisions ever
look wrong rather than merely generous.
